optimal-engine/agents-and-workflows:
Optimal Engine does not run agents or call tools itself.
It is the memory and the rules an agent works from: what to read first, what is open, what it may do, and a record of what it did.
Any agent reaches it over HTTP, the `optimal` CLI, or the MCP server; see [CLI, SDKs and MCP](/docs/optimal-engine/cli-sdks-mcp).

## Start of a session: boot

```bash
optimal boot -w default:notes
```

`GET /api/boot?workspace=` returns, in one call:

- today's date and the current rhythm note;
- loops that are overdue or due today;
- recent decisions and stale items;
- the brief and the operating protocol;
- the organization policy the workspace follows.

An agent should call it before anything else in a session.

## Daily operation

| Route | CLI | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/brief` | `optimal brief` | Ranked items that need a decision today |
| `GET /api/loops`, `POST /api/loops` | `optimal loops`, `optimal loops add` | Open loops: commitments, replies owed, follow-ups, payments, decisions needed |
| `POST /api/loops/extract` | `optimal loops extract` | Find new loops in recent sources |
| `POST /api/loops/:id/close`, `drop`, `reopen` | `optimal loops close` | Change a loop's state |
| `GET /api/rhythm/current` | `optimal today` | The daily, weekly, or monthly note |
| `GET /api/protocol`, `PUT /api/protocol` | `optimal protocol` | The protocol an agent follows in this workspace |

## Rules for what an agent may do

### Authority

Authority answers allow, ask, or deny for an action on a resource, such as reading, writing, exporting, erasing, or syncing.
Deny wins, and anything without a rule is denied.

```bash
optimal authority decide --action export --resource "optimal://default:notes/..." -w default:notes
```

| Route | What it does |
|---|---|
| `POST /api/authority/decide` | Ask for a decision |
| `GET /api/authority/effective` | The rules that apply to a subject |
| `POST /api/authority/requests` | Ask a person to approve an action |
| `/api/authority/policies`, `/api/authority/grants` | Manage rules and time-limited grants |

Turn it on with `OPTIMAL_AUTHORITY_MODE`: `off` by default, `observe` to record decisions without blocking, or `enforce`.

### Organization policy

`PUT /api/org-section` sets rules once for the organization.
Every workspace reads them through `GET /api/org-policy`, cannot change them, and receives them in `boot` and `assemble`.

### Pre-send check

`POST /api/signals/check` (`optimal check`) checks a draft message against its receiver and channel, and suggests a shorter version.

## Records of work

| Route | What it does |
|---|---|
| `POST /api/agent-actions`, `GET /api/agent-actions/:id` | Record an agent's action, and read it with its linked evidence |
| `POST /api/sessions/commit` | Store a finished chat as an episode; what it learned goes to claim review |
| `GET /api/viability` | A health report on the workspace as an operating system, with alerts |

## Scheduled analyses and jobs

The Engine runs six analyses on a schedule: `promises`, `workspace_population`, `meeting_archive`, `file_audit`, `storage_usage`, and `retention_sweep`.

| Route | What it does |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/analyses` | Their reports |
| `POST /api/analyses/run` | Run one now (`admin`) |
| `GET /api/jobs` | The job queue |
| `GET /api/jobs/dead`, `POST /api/jobs/dead/:id/replay` | Failed jobs, and retrying one |

## Webhooks and live updates

A subscription says what an agent or person wants pushed to them: anything in a workspace, one node, a topic, or one audience.
Create one with `POST /api/subscriptions`; it can be paused, resumed, and deleted.
The Engine pushes matching items over `GET /api/surface/stream`, a server-sent event stream, and to a webhook when the subscription's `metadata` has a `webhook_url`.
`POST /api/subscriptions/:id/test-webhook` sends a test delivery.

> **Note: Workflows and skill packages**
>
> The Engine records workflow traces and can promote repeated ones into skill packages (`mix optimal.skills`).
> Those are records for review and retrieval.
> The Engine does not run a skill package as code, and it has no agent registry or delegation between agents.
optimal-engine/api:
| | |
|---|---|
| Base URL | `http://127.0.0.1:4200/api` on a self-hosted Engine. `/v1/...` is an alias of `/api/...`. |
| On MIOSA | `https://api.miosa.ai/api/v1/engines/<engine id>/engine-api/api/...` with an Engine client key; see [Optimal Engine on MIOSA](/docs/optimal-engine/miosa#call-the-engine-api) |
| API version | `v1` |
| Auth | `Authorization: Bearer <key>` or `X-API-Key: <key>` |
| Body | JSON with `Content-Type: application/json` |
| Errors | `{"error": "<code>"}`, sometimes with a `detail` |

The Engine has about 300 routes.
This page covers the ones most apps and agents use.
The complete list, with the grant each route needs, is generated from the router into [`docs/reference/api.md`](https://github.com/Miosa-osa/OptimalEngine/blob/main/docs/reference/api.md), and a test fails whenever the two disagree.

```bash
E=http://127.0.0.1:4200
K="Authorization: Bearer $OPTIMAL_ENGINE_API_KEY"
```

## Keys and errors

When `OPTIMAL_AUTH_REQUIRED=true`, every route needs a key, including `/api/health`.

| Status | `error` | When |
|---|---|---|
| 400 | `invalid_json`, `invalid_parameter`, `workspace_required` | The request is malformed, or a key limited to named workspaces did not name one |
| 401 | `missing_api_key`, `invalid_api_key`, `api_key_revoked`, `api_key_expired` | The key is missing or not usable |
| 403 | `workspace_scope_denied` | The key does not cover that workspace |
| 403 | `permission_scope_denied` | The key does not have the scope the route needs |
| 404 | `not found`, `workspace not found` | No such route, or a workspace of another tenant |
| 413 | `request_too_large` | The body is over 8 MB |
| 426 | `client_incompatible` | An `optimal` CLI or MCP server of another major version |
| 429 | `rate_limited` | Over the key's rate limit; the body has `retry_after_ms` |
| 503 | `busy` | The store is busy, for example right after boot; retry after `Retry-After` |

### Rate limits

Each key has its own budget per minute, set by the [size profile](/docs/optimal-engine/operations#sizing): 1,200 requests a minute on the default `business` profile.
Requests without a valid key share their IP address's budget.
Every response carries `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, and `X-RateLimit-Reset`.
`/api/health`, `/api/status`, and `/api/metrics/prometheus` are not counted.

### Paging

List routes take `offset` and `limit` (1 to 200, default 50) and answer with:

```json
"pagination": {"offset": 0, "limit": 50, "total": 132, "has_more": true}
```

## Engine

| Route | Returns |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/health` | `status` (`up`, `degraded`, `down`), `checks`, `warnings`, and the release. `?full=true` runs ten store diagnostics for one workspace. |
| `GET /api/status` | The same, plus `api_version` |
| `GET /api/version` | `version`, `git_sha`, `build_timestamp`, `release_channel`, `api_version`, `expected_migration`, `capabilities` |
| `GET /api/metrics` | JSON counters, latencies, and size gauges |
| `GET /api/metrics/prometheus` | Prometheus text format |
| `GET /api/auth/whoami` | The key's own scopes and workspaces |

## Workspaces and nodes

### Create a workspace

`POST /api/workspaces`

```bash
curl -s -X POST $E/api/workspaces -H "$K" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"slug": "sales", "name": "Sales"}'
```

| Field | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `slug` | yes | Lowercase name, unique in the tenant |
| `name` | yes | Display name |
| `description` | no | |
| `external_id` | no | Your own id for this workspace, unique in the tenant |

`201` returns the workspace: `id` (`default:sales`), `tenant_id`, `slug`, `name`, `status`, `created_at`.
Errors: `400` for a missing or invalid slug or name, `409 slug_taken`, `409 external_id_taken`.

| Route | What it does |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/workspaces` | List workspaces, paged |
| `GET /api/workspaces/:id`, `PATCH /api/workspaces/:id` | Read or rename one |
| `POST /api/workspaces/:id/archive` | Archive it; its data is kept |
| `GET /api/workspaces/:id/config`, `PATCH ...` | Workspace settings |

### Create a node

`POST /api/nodes` with `{"name", "kind", "slug", "workspace", "description"}` answers `{"ok": true, "id", "slug", "kind"}`.
`kind` is one of the node kinds in [Concepts](/docs/optimal-engine/concepts#topology).

## Ingest

`POST /api/ingest` stores text as a source.
See [Sources and ingestion](/docs/optimal-engine/ingestion) for the fields, files, chat sessions, Notion, and connectors.

```bash
curl -s -X POST $E/api/ingest -H "$K" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"workspace": "default:sales", "title": "Auth decision", "text": "Decided: refresh-token rotation ships in v2."}'
```

```json
{"ok": true, "signal_id": "...", "genre": "...", "type": "...", "entities": [], "source_package_id": "..."}
```

## Search

`GET /api/search?q=&workspace=&limit=&offset=&mode=&type=&as_of=`

```bash
curl -s "$E/api/search?q=refresh%20token&workspace=default:sales&limit=5" -H "$K"
```

```json
{
  "query": "refresh token",
  "results": [
    {
      "id": "...",
      "title": "Auth decision",
      "uri": "optimal://...",
      "content": "Decided: refresh-token rotation ships in v2.",
      "l0_abstract": "...",
      "score": 0.82,
      "workspace_id": "default:sales",
      "inherited": false
    }
  ],
  "pagination": {"offset": 0, "limit": 5, "total": 1, "has_more": false}
}
```

`mode=hybrid` answers `503 hybrid_unavailable` when no embedding model answers.
A bad `as_of` answers `400`.

| Route | What it does |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/grep?q=` | Matching chunks, with `intent`, `scale`, `modality`, `literal`, and `path` filters |
| `GET /api/read?uri=&tier=` | One item by its `optimal://` URI; `tier` is `l0`, `l1`, or `full` |
| `GET /api/recall/who`, `when`, `where`, `owns`, `actions` | Targeted recall over people, time, places, ownership, and actions |
| `GET /api/profile` | A workspace profile: ground truth, recent activity, and top entities |
| `GET /api/graph`, `/api/graph/hubs`, `/api/graph/clusters` | The knowledge graph |

## Ask and assemble

`POST /api/rag` returns context for one question; `GET /api/rag/stream` streams it as server-sent events.
`POST /api/assemble` returns a tiered context package for an agent.
See [Memory and retrieval](/docs/optimal-engine/memory-and-retrieval#ask) for fields and responses.

```bash
curl -s -X POST $E/api/rag -H "$K" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"query": "What did we decide about auth?", "workspace": "default:sales", "format": "markdown", "bandwidth": "small"}'

curl -N "$E/api/rag/stream?query=auth%20decision&workspace=default:sales" -H "$K"
```

optimal-engine/cli-sdks-mcp:
Every interface below talks to the same HTTP API, so a workspace looks the same from each.
All of them install from a checkout of [Miosa-osa/OptimalEngine](https://github.com/Miosa-osa/OptimalEngine).

| Interface | For | Where |
|---|---|---|
| `optimal` CLI (also `oe`) | People and agents in a terminal | `apps/cli` |
| MCP server | Agent clients such as Claude Code and Codex | `apps/mcp` |
| Mix tasks | Operators on the Engine's own machine | `lib/mix/tasks` |
| TypeScript client | Apps | `sdks/typescript` |
| Python client | Apps and scripts | `sdks/python` |

> **Note: Not on npm or PyPI**
>
> The clients and the MCP server are not published to npm or PyPI.
> Build them from the repository as shown below.

## The optimal CLI

A single shell script that needs `sh`, `curl` 7.55 or newer, and `awk`.
It sends the key to curl on standard input, so the key never shows in a process list, and it never prints the key.

```bash
apps/cli/install.sh            # installs optimal and oe into /usr/local/bin or ~/.local/bin
optimal --version
```

### Point it at an Engine

Settings are read in this order, first match wins:

1. Flags: `--api <url>`, `--key-file <path>`, `-w <workspace>`, `--profile <name>`.
2. A named profile, from `--profile` or `OPTIMAL_PROFILE`.
3. Environment: `OPTIMAL_ENGINE_URL`, `OPTIMAL_ENGINE_API_KEY` or `OPTIMAL_ENGINE_API_KEY_FILE`, `OPTIMAL_WORKSPACE`.
4. The default profile, `~/.config/optimal/profile`.
5. `http://127.0.0.1:4200`.

A profile file holds the same settings:

```text
url=http://127.0.0.1:4200
key_file=/home/me/.config/optimal/key
workspace=default:notes
```

`optimal doctor` reports where each setting came from and whether the Engine answers.
On MIOSA, `miosa engine connect` writes this profile for you; see [Optimal Engine on MIOSA](/docs/optimal-engine/miosa#from-a-terminal).

### Commands

| Group | Commands |
|---|---|
| Session | `boot`, `today`, `fires`, `brief`, `protocol`, `commitments` |
| Loops | `loops list`, `loops add`, `loops close`, `loops drop`, `loops reopen`, `loops extract` |
| Retrieve | `search` (`find`), `grep`, `assemble`, `read`, `ask` (`rag`), `reconstruct`, `memory`, `claims`, `review` |
| Record | `capture`, `aware`, `note`, `lesson`, `decision`, `task`, `close`, `remember` |
| Chats and policy | `session commit`, `session list`, `session show`, `policy`, `org-section` |
| Rules | `routing`, `authority effective`, `authority decide`, `authority request`, `authority export` |
| Setup and health | `init`, `size`, `viability`, `chain`, `check`, `analyses`, `jobs` |
| Engine | `status`, `health`, `version`, `doctor`, `url`, `workspaces`, `organizations`, `whoami` |
| Any route | `api <METHOD> /api/<path> [json]` |

```bash
optimal capture "Decided: annual plans get two months free." -w default:notes --title "Pricing"
optimal search "annual plans" -w default:notes -n 5
optimal ask "What did we decide about pricing?" -w default:notes
optimal api GET /api/version
```

Common options: `-n` for a limit, `--as-of` for a point in time, `--mode lexical|hybrid|auto`, `--field a.b` to print one field, and `--raw` for unformatted JSON.

| Exit code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | Done |
| 1 | Failed |
| 64 | Wrong usage |
| 65 | The Engine's answer could not be read |
| 69 | The Engine did not answer |
| 77 | The key was refused (401 or 403) |
| 78 | A setting is wrong, the command was refused, or the client is too old (426) |

## MCP server

A stdio MCP server over the same API, for agent clients.
It needs Node 20 or newer.

```bash
cd apps/mcp
npm ci && npm run build
```

It reads the same settings as the CLI, from the environment or a profile, once when it starts.
Restart it after the key changes.

Register it with Claude Code:

```bash
claude mcp add --scope user \
  --env OPTIMAL_ENGINE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4200 \
  --env OPTIMAL_ENGINE_API_KEY_FILE=/home/me/.config/optimal/key \
  --env OPTIMAL_WORKSPACE=default:notes \
  optimal-engine -- node /path/to/OptimalEngine/apps/mcp/dist/index.js
```

Give it a key with only what its agent needs, for example `read` and `write` on one workspace.

| Group | Tools |
|---|---|
| Operating loop | `boot`, `brief`, `protocol`, `loops_list`, `loops_add`, `loops_close` |
| Retrieve | `search`, `grep`, `ask`, `assemble`, `read`, `recall`, `profile`, `wiki_get`, `workspaces` |
| Record | `capture`, `record`, `close`, `add_memory`, `forget_memory` |
| Chats and policy | `session_commit`, `sessions_list`, `session_get`, `org_policy` |
| Rules and checks | `authority_decide`, `authority_effective`, `check_draft`, `viability`, `action_step`, `action_chain` |
| Rendering | `render_context`, `render_specs` |

## Mix tasks

On the Engine's own machine, a checkout has `mix optimal.*` tasks that work on the store directly.
Useful ones:

| Task | What it does |
|---|---|
| `mix optimal.auth` | Mint, list, revoke, and delete API keys |
| `mix optimal.bootstrap` | Compile, migrate, and load the sample workspace |
| `mix optimal.status`, `mix optimal.health` | Liveness, and ten store diagnostics |
| `mix optimal.ingest`, `mix optimal.ingest_workspace` | Ingest text or a folder |
| `mix optimal.import_notion` | Import a Notion export |
| `mix optimal.connector`, `mix optimal.pull` | Set up and run app connectors |
| `mix optimal.search`, `mix optimal.rag`, `mix optimal.assemble` | Read from the command line |
| `mix optimal.claims`, `mix optimal.facts` | Review claims and list facts |
| `mix optimal.backup`, `mix optimal.restore`, `mix optimal.migrate` | Operations; see [Operations](/docs/optimal-engine/operations) |
| `mix optimal.embed_backfill`, `mix optimal.index` | Embed missing chunks, or reindex |
| `mix optimal.compliance` | Data export, erasure, legal holds, and retention |
| `mix optimal.conformance` | Run the conformance suite against a live Engine |

`docs/guides/mix-tasks.md` in the repository lists all of them.

## TypeScript client

```bash
cd sdks/typescript
npm install && npm run build
```

```ts
import { OptimalEngine } from "@optimal-engine/client";

const engine = new OptimalEngine({
  baseUrl: "http://127.0.0.1:4200",
  apiKey: process.env.OPTIMAL_ENGINE_API_KEY,
  workspace: "default:notes",
});

await engine.ingest("Decided: annual plans get two months free.", { title: "Pricing" });
const hits = await engine.search("annual plans");
const context = await engine.ask("What did we decide about pricing?");
console.log(context.envelope.body, context.envelope.sources);
```

It also has `grep`, `assemble`, `profile`, `createNode`, and sub-clients for `memory`, `workspaces`, `wiki`, `recall`, `subscriptions`, `surface`, and `render`.
Adapters for the Vercel AI SDK and the OpenAI Agents SDK are at `@optimal-engine/client/adapters/ai-sdk` and `/adapters/openai-agents`.

## Python client

```bash
pip install ./sdks/python
```

```python
from optimal_engine import OptimalEngine

engine = OptimalEngine(base_url="http://127.0.0.1:4200", workspace="default:notes", api_key="oe_...")
results = engine.search("annual plans")
memory = engine.memory.create(content="Customer Example Co renews in March.")
```

It needs Python 3.10 or newer, and has a sync `OptimalEngine` and an async `AsyncOptimalEngine`.
It covers search, grep, recall, memory, and workspaces.

> **Caution: Python ask**
>
> In the current Python client, `ask()` reads the answer from the wrong field and returns an empty `body`.
> Call `POST /api/rag` directly, or use the TypeScript client, until it is fixed.
optimal-engine/concepts:
Optimal Engine keeps three things apart: the evidence you gave it, the truth that was accepted from that evidence, and the views it builds for a reader.
Every object below belongs to one of those three.

## Topology

```text
Tenant / Organization
  -> Workspaces
      -> Nodes
          -> sources, signals, memories, wiki pages
```

| Object | What it is |
|---|---|
| Tenant / Organization | The top scope. It owns workspaces and holds the organization policy every workspace reads. |
| Workspace | One walled section with its own nodes, sources, memories, loops, and rhythm. A key can be limited to some workspaces. |
| Node | A typed thing inside a workspace. |
| Node relationship | A typed link between two nodes. |

A workspace id is `<tenant>:<slug>`, for example `default:sales` for the workspace `sales` in the `default` tenant.
The workspace `default` always exists.

Node kinds, as `POST /api/nodes` accepts them: `unit`, `team`, `project`, `entity`, `domain`, `department`, `operation`, `learning`, `person`, `product`, `partnership`, `context`.

Each new workspace also gets the standard node types the setup and topology tools use: `entity`, `division`, `department`, `team`, `role`, `project`, `process`, `task`, `operation`, `learning`, `person`, `customer`, `product`, `partnership`, `context`.

Relationship types: `parent_child`, `depends_on`, `blocks`, `references`, `collaborates_with`, `sequence_before`, `instance_of`, `owns`, `participates_in`, `supports`.

A project is only one kind of node.
Model ongoing work, such as hiring or support, as an `operation` node instead.

## From a source to memory

```text
source -> signal -> claim -> fact -> context package
```

| Object | What it is |
|---|---|
| Source package | The raw input, kept with its metadata, trust label, and retention state. It is never rewritten. |
| Signal | The classified unit the Engine works on. |
| Context | The indexed unit search returns: a signal, a resource, a memory, or a skill file. |
| Claim | An assertion the Engine found in a source, with a link back to it. A claim is pending until it is reviewed. |
| Fact | An accepted claim, with its evidence, confidence, precision, and the time it is valid for. |
| Memory object | The meaning around facts, sources, and time, such as an episode from a chat session. |
| Derivation ledger | The record of which source each claim, fact, and memory came from. |

### Signals

Every input is classified on five separate dimensions:

```text
Signal = Mode + Genre + Type + Format + Structure
```

Keeping them separate lets the Engine route, parse, and retrieve a meeting transcript differently from a spec or a code file.
Classification is rule-based and runs without a language model.

### Claims and facts

The Engine never treats an extracted sentence as true on its own.
A claim becomes a fact in one of two ways:

- A person or key with the `claims:review` grant promotes it.
- The workspace's promotion rule promotes it automatically.

The rule is set with `OPTIMAL_CLAIM_PROMOTION_MODE`:

| Mode | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `auto_threshold` (default) | Promotes a claim whose score reaches the workspace threshold, 0.85 by default |
| `manual` | Every claim waits for review |
| `agent_review` | Currently behaves like `manual` |

A promoted claim is kept and marked `promoted`, so the evidence trail stays complete.
A newer fact can supersede an older one, and the older one stays readable as history.

### Versioned memories

Alongside the claim lifecycle, the Engine keeps a simpler memory store you write to directly with `POST /api/memory`.
Each memory has versions, and memories link to each other with `updates`, `extends`, `derives`, `contradicts`, or `cites`.
Forgetting a memory hides it without deleting it; deleting is a separate, permanent call.

`POST /api/memory/remember` is the gated way in: it scores a new memory for novelty and salience, then adds it, updates a similar one, skips it, or proposes it as a claim.

## Reading the memory

| Object | What it is |
|---|---|
| Context package | What one reader may see for one task: the facts and memories used, their sources, confidence, and validity. It is a view, not truth. |
| Active memory pool | A working memory for one task, with the observations made during it. |
| Retrieval strategy | `tiered`, `reconstructive`, or `hybrid`. See [Memory and retrieval](/docs/optimal-engine/memory-and-retrieval). |

## Projections

The Engine's database is the source of truth.
Everything else is a projection of it:

- **Workspace files**: each workspace has a folder with `nodes/`, `.wiki/`, `assets/`, and `architectures/`. Editing a file there comes back in as a new source, not as a direct change to the truth.
- **Wiki pages**: curated pages with citations, kept in `.wiki/`.
- **Workspace bundles**: a whole workspace exported as one file and imported into another Engine.
- **The API, CLI, and MCP server**: the same state, read by people and agents.

## Governance

| Object | What it is |
|---|---|
| API key | Identifies the caller. It carries scopes and a list of workspaces it may use. |
| Authority | Allow, ask, or deny rules for reading, searching, writing, exporting, erasing, and syncing. Deny wins. It runs in `off`, `observe`, or `enforce` mode. |
| Organization policy | Rules set once for the organization that every workspace reads and cannot change. |
| Security labels and partitions | Labels such as `confidential` on rows, and the partitions a key may read. |

> **Note: Words in the API**
>
> The API uses the same names as this page: `workspace`, `node`, `claim`, `memory`, `context_package`.
> URIs in results use the `optimal://` scheme.
optimal-engine/ingestion:
Every input is kept as a source package first, then classified, split into chunks, indexed, and mined for claims.
The original is never rewritten, so every fact can point back to the source it came from.

## Ways in

| Input | Route or command |
|---|---|
| Text | `POST /api/ingest`, `optimal capture`, `mix optimal.ingest` |
| A file | `POST /api/assets` with the bytes as base64 |
| A folder of files | `mix optimal.ingest_workspace` |
| A finished chat | `POST /api/sessions/commit`, `optimal session commit` |
| A durable memory | `POST /api/memory`, `POST /api/memory/remember`, `optimal remember` |
| A Notion export | `POST /api/import/notion`, `mix optimal.import_notion` |
| Many records at once | `POST /api/batch/import/signals`, `POST /api/batch/import/memories` |
| An app | Connectors, below |
| Another Engine's workspace | A workspace bundle; see [Operations](/docs/optimal-engine/operations#move-a-workspace) |

## Text

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4200/api/ingest \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPTIMAL_ENGINE_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "workspace": "default:notes",
    "title": "Pricing decision",
    "text": "Decided: annual plans get two months free from March.",
    "node": "pricing",
    "extract_claims": true
  }'
```

| Field | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `text` | yes | The content |
| `workspace` | no | Workspace id; `default` when left out |
| `title` | no | Title shown in results |
| `genre` | no | Override the genre the Engine would pick |
| `node` | no | Node slug the source belongs to |
| `extract_claims` | no | `true` by default |

The response is `{"ok": true, "signal_id", "genre", "type", "entities", "source_package_id"}`.
A missing `text` answers `400`; a source the pipeline cannot take answers `422` with `ok: false` and an `error`.

## Files

`POST /api/assets` takes a file as `content_base64` with its filename.
The Engine stores the bytes, hashed, under the workspace's `assets/` folder, or in S3-compatible storage when `OPTIMAL_ASSET_STORAGE=s3`.

| Kind | Extensions | Text comes from |
|---|---|---|
| Markdown and text | `.md` `.txt` `.rst` `.adoc` `.log` | the file |
| Data | `.yaml` `.yml` `.toml` `.json` `.csv` `.tsv` | the file |
| Web | `.html` `.htm` `.xhtml` | the file |
| Code | about 37 languages, such as `.ex` `.py` `.js` `.ts` `.go` `.rs` `.java` `.sql` | the file |
| Office | `.docx` `.pptx` `.xlsx` | the file |
| PDF | `.pdf` | `pdftotext` |
| Images | `.png` `.jpg` `.jpeg` `.gif` `.webp` `.svg` | `tesseract`, plus a description from the vision model |
| Audio | `.mp3` `.wav` `.m4a` `.ogg` `.flac` | a whisper.cpp server |
| Video | `.mp4` `.mov` `.webm` `.mkv` | `ffmpeg` keyframes and audio |

An unknown extension is read as plain text.
When a tool is missing, the file is kept with its metadata and a warning such as `ffmpeg not on PATH`, and you can parse it again later.

## Chat sessions

Commit a finished conversation so its lessons become memory:

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4200/api/sessions/commit \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPTIMAL_ENGINE_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "workspace": "default:notes",
    "correlation_id": "chat-2026-10-23-01",
    "title": "Renewal planning",
    "messages": [
      {"role": "user", "content": "When is the supplier renewal?"},
      {"role": "assistant", "content": "The call moved to the 14th."}
    ],
    "learned": ["The supplier renewal call is on the 14th."]
  }'
```

The chat is stored as an episode.
Each `learned` item, up to 50, becomes a proposed claim in the review queue.
The response (`201`) has the `session_id`, its `uri`, the `summary`, and the `message_count`.
Read sessions back with `GET /api/sessions` and `GET /api/sessions/:id`.

## Notion exports

Export a Notion workspace as **Markdown & CSV**, then send the zip:

```bash
mix optimal.import_notion ./notion-export.zip --workspace default:notes
```

Over HTTP, `POST /api/import/notion` takes the zip as the request body and starts a job; follow it with `GET /api/import/notion/:job_id`.
Each page, database, and row becomes its own item with an `optimal://<workspace>/notion/<id>` URI, and page hierarchy and links become graph edges.
The importer checks sizes before it unpacks anything, refuses ZIP64 archives, and never turns an entry name into a path on disk.

## Apps (connectors)

A connector pulls records from an app on a schedule and stores them as sources.
It only reads; nothing is written back to the app.

| Group | Apps |
|---|---|
| Mail, files, and docs | Gmail, Google Drive, Notion, Dropbox, OneDrive, Confluence, a local sources folder |
| Chat and meetings | Slack, Microsoft Teams, Zoom, Fathom |
| Work tracking and code | GitHub, Linear, Jira |
| CRM and business | HubSpot, Salesforce, HighLevel, Stripe |
| Publishing and forms | beehiiv, Jotform |

Set `CONNECTOR_KEY` before you add one: it encrypts the app keys the Engine stores.

```bash
mix optimal.connector list
mix optimal.pull
```

Over HTTP, `GET` and `POST /api/connectors` list and add connectors, and `POST /api/connectors/:id/run` runs one now.
`docs/guides/connectors.md` in the repository lists what each one pulls and how it signs in.
Pulled records are stored as database rows with `optimal://connectors/<kind>/<id>` URIs, not as files, unless the connector is set to write files.

> **Note: How deep a connector goes**
>
> Every connector pulls the records its guide lists.
> Downloading every attachment and binary file is not complete for every app yet.

## Limits

| Limit | Value |
|---|---|
| JSON request body | 8 MB |
| Import file | 1 GiB (`OPTIMAL_IMPORT_MAX_BYTES`) |
| Workspace bundle | 5 GiB (`OPTIMAL_BUNDLE_MAX_BYTES`) |
| Text sent to the embedding model | 6,000 characters per chunk |
| Learned items per chat session | 50 |
optimal-engine/install:
This page covers a self-hosted Engine.
A managed Engine on MIOSA is set up for you; see [Optimal Engine on MIOSA](/docs/optimal-engine/miosa).

## Requirements

| Need | Version or note |
|---|---|
| Erlang/OTP | 27 or newer. Avoid OTP 28.0 to 28.2; the Docker image uses 28.5. |
| Elixir | 1.17 or newer |
| Build tools | git, a C toolchain, CMake. The image also installs zlib, zstd, lz4, bz2, snappy, and SQLite headers. |
| macOS | `brew install snappy` |
| Embeddings (optional) | [Ollama](https://ollama.com/) with `nomic-embed-text`, or any OpenAI-compatible embeddings endpoint |
| Media parsing (optional) | `pdftotext` for PDF, `tesseract` for image text, `ffmpeg` for video, a whisper.cpp server for audio |

Without an embedding model the Engine still works: search is full-text only, and a backfill embeds everything once a model is set up.
Without a media tool, a file of that kind is stored with its metadata and a warning instead of its text.

## Install

### From a checkout

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Miosa-osa/OptimalEngine.git
cd OptimalEngine
mix deps.get
mix optimal.auth mint --name "root" --workspace '*'
OPTIMAL_API_ENABLED=true OPTIMAL_AUTH_REQUIRED=true mix run --no-halt
```

`make bootstrap` (or `mix optimal.bootstrap`) compiles, runs migrations, and loads the bundled `sample-workspace/` so you have data to try.

### With Docker

`deploy/Dockerfile.engine` builds an OTP release on Elixir 1.19.5 and OTP 28.5.

| Image default | Value |
|---|---|
| User | `optimal`, UID 1000, not root |
| Data | `/data`, the only volume. The database is `/data/.optimal/index.db`. |
| Port | `4200`, bound to `0.0.0.0` inside the container |
| API | On, with keys required (`OPTIMAL_AUTH_REQUIRED=true`) |
| Embeddings | `OLLAMA_HOST=http://host.docker.internal:11434` |
| Health check | `GET /api/health` with `Authorization: Bearer $OPTIMAL_ENGINE_API_KEY` |

Set `OPTIMAL_ENGINE_API_KEY` on the container, or the health check runs without a key and the container reports unhealthy.
On Linux, `host.docker.internal` does not resolve by default; point `OLLAMA_HOST` at the host's address.

### With Docker Compose

```bash
cd deploy
cp env.example .env
# Set OPTIMAL_BOOTSTRAP_KEY and OPTIMAL_ENGINE_API_KEY to the same oe_ key.
docker compose up --build
```

Compose publishes the Engine on `127.0.0.1:4200` and keeps data in the `optimal_data` volume.
For a public server, add the production overlay, which puts Caddy with automatic TLS in front and keeps the Engine port private:

```bash
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.prod.yml up -d
```

Set `DOMAIN` and `LETSENCRYPT_EMAIL` in `.env` first.

> **Caution: The storage overlay**
>
> `deploy/docker-compose.storage.yml` also starts Postgres, NATS, Valkey, Qdrant, and OpenBao.
> In 0.3.10 the Engine only uses its S3-compatible storage from that set.
> The others have no adapter yet and report `adapter_missing`.

### As a release

```bash
MIX_ENV=prod mix release optimal
OPTIMAL_API_ENABLED=true OPTIMAL_AUTH_REQUIRED=true _build/prod/rel/optimal/bin/optimal start
```

`bin/optimal maintenance <task>` runs maintenance with the API off; see [Operations](/docs/optimal-engine/operations#upgrades).

## Settings

The Engine reads its settings from environment variables at boot.
An invalid value stops the boot with a message that names the variable.

### Server and keys

| Variable | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `OPTIMAL_API_ENABLED` | off (image: on) | Only the value `true` starts the HTTP API |
| `OPTIMAL_API_PORT` | `4200` | Port |
| `OPTIMAL_API_INTERFACE` | `127.0.0.1` (image: `0.0.0.0`) | Address to bind |
| `OPTIMAL_AUTH_REQUIRED` | `false` (image: `true`) | Require an API key on every request. Takes `true` or `false` only. |
| `OPTIMAL_BOOTSTRAP_KEY` | none | Registers a first key at boot, in the form `oe_<24 hex>_<secret of 32+ characters>`. Changing it rotates the key. |
| `OPTIMAL_BOOTSTRAP_SCOPES` | `read,write` | Scopes of the bootstrap key |
| `OPTIMAL_BOOTSTRAP_WORKSPACES` | `*` | Workspaces of the bootstrap key |
| `OPTIMAL_BOOTSTRAP_TENANT` | `default` | Tenant of the bootstrap key |
| `OPTIMAL_REFUSE_OPEN_NETWORK` | off | Refuse to start when bound beyond loopback with keys off |
| `OPTIMAL_OPEN_NETWORK_ACKNOWLEDGED` | off | You run keys-off behind a proxy that authenticates every request |
| `OPTIMAL_SIZE_PROFILE` | `business` | Size profile; see [Operations](/docs/optimal-engine/operations#sizing) |

### Paths and storage

| Variable | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `OPTIMAL_ENGINE_ROOT` | the working directory (image: `/data`) | Root of the workspace folders |
| `OPTIMAL_ENGINE_DB` | `.optimal/index.db` | SQLite database file |
| `OPTIMAL_ENGINE_CACHE` | `.optimal/cache` | Cache, including stored embeddings |
| `OPTIMAL_BACKUP_DIR` | `backups/` next to the database | Where backups are written |
| `OPTIMAL_KNOWLEDGE_BACKEND` | `ets` | Graph projection: `ets` in memory, or `rocksdb` on disk |
| `OPTIMAL_ASSET_STORAGE` | filesystem | `s3` keeps uploaded file bytes in S3-compatible storage |
| `OPTIMAL_S3_ENDPOINT`, `OPTIMAL_S3_BUCKET`, `OPTIMAL_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `OPTIMAL_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` | none | S3, MinIO, R2, or Garage. Also `OPTIMAL_S3_REGION` (`us-east-1`) and `OPTIMAL_S3_PREFIX`. |

### Secrets

Each is 64 hex characters; generate one with `openssl rand -hex 32`.

| Variable | Needed when |
|---|---|
| `CONNECTOR_KEY` | You set up app connectors or replication peers. It encrypts their stored keys. |
| `OPTIMAL_AUTHORITY_KEY` | Recommended always. It protects the signing keys of authority grants. |
| `OPTIMAL_BACKUP_KEY` | You send backups offsite. It encrypts them. |

### Embeddings

| Variable | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `OLLAMA_HOST` | `http://localhost:11434` | Ollama server |
| `OPTIMAL_EMBED_MODEL` | `nomic-embed-text` | Embedding model, 768 dimensions |
| `OPTIMAL_EMBED_URL` | none | Another endpoint. A path ending in `/api/embed` speaks Ollama; anything else speaks OpenAI `/v1/embeddings`. |
| `OPTIMAL_EMBED_DIMENSIONS` | `768` | Vector size of that model |
| `OPTIMAL_EMBED_API_KEY` or `OPTIMAL_EMBED_API_KEY_FILE` | none | Key for that endpoint, read per request and never stored |
| `OPTIMAL_GENERATE_MODEL` | `qwen3:1.7b` | Small model used to curate wiki pages and summarize sessions |
| `OPTIMAL_VLM_MODEL` | `qwen2.5-vl` | Vision model that describes images |

### Behavior

| Variable | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `OPTIMAL_CLAIM_PROMOTION_MODE` | `auto_threshold` | `auto_threshold`, `manual`, or `agent_review`; see [Concepts](/docs/optimal-engine/concepts#claims-and-facts) |
| `OPTIMAL_AUTHORITY_MODE` | `off` | `off`, `observe` (log decisions), or `enforce` |
| `OPTIMAL_ENGINE_SCOPE` | `org` | `workspace` limits the Engine to `OPTIMAL_ENGINE_WORKSPACE` |
| `OPTIMAL_IMPORT_MAX_BYTES` | 1 GiB | Largest import file |
| `OPTIMAL_BUNDLE_MAX_BYTES` | 5 GiB | Largest workspace bundle |
| `OPTIMAL_RELEASE_CHANNEL` | `dev` | `dev`, `stable`, `beta`, or `pinned`, as `/api/version` reports it |

`deploy/env.example` in the repository lists every variable with a comment.

## Where data lives

SQLite is the store.
It holds full-text search, vectors, and every record, so one file plus the folders around it is the whole Engine.

```text
<OPTIMAL_ENGINE_ROOT>/          workspace folders: nodes/, .wiki/, assets/
.optimal/index.db               the database (with -wal and -shm files)
.optimal/cache/                 cache and stored embeddings
.optimal/backups/               local backups
.optimal/knowledge-rocksdb/     graph projection, when the rocksdb backend is on
```

`GET /api/stores` lists the 13 logical stores and which provider backs each one.

> **Note: PostgreSQL**
>
> A PostgreSQL store exists, but it needs a build compiled with `OPTIMAL_STORE=postgres`, and moving an existing Engine onto it is not supported yet.
> The Docker image is SQLite only.
> Run `mix optimal.postgres.check` to see its state on your build.

## API keys and scopes

Send a key as `Authorization: Bearer <key>` or `X-API-Key: <key>`.
Keys look like `oe_<id>_<secret>`; the Engine keeps only a bcrypt hash of the secret.

Mint keys from the checkout:

```bash
mix optimal.auth mint --name "agent" --workspace default:notes --scope read --scope write
mix optimal.auth list
mix optimal.auth revoke <id>
```

Or over HTTP with an `admin` key: `POST /api/auth/keys` with `{"name", "scopes", "workspace_scope", "expires_at"}`.
A key can only mint keys narrower than itself.
`GET /api/auth/whoami` shows a key's own scopes and workspaces.

| Scope | Allows |
|---|---|
| `read`, `write` | Reading and writing in the key's workspaces |
| `admin` | Keys, backups, maintenance, and other operator routes |
| `claims:review` | Promoting and rejecting claims |
| `topology:write` | Changing workspaces and nodes |
| `connectors:write` | Setting up app connectors |
| `sync` | Replication |
| `data:admin` | App data collections |
| `authority:read`, `authority:enforce`, `authority:approve`, `authority:issue`, `authority:admin` | Authority rules and grants |
| `*` | Everything |

> **Caution: Keys off means open**
>
> With `OPTIMAL_AUTH_REQUIRED=false`, a request with no key acts as the local operator and can do anything.
> That is fine on `127.0.0.1`.
> Bound to any other address, the Engine logs an error at boot and every 10 minutes, and `/api/health` warns `auth_open_on_network`.
> A tunnel or proxy in front of a loopback Engine is not detected, so turn keys on before you publish it.
optimal-engine/memory-and-retrieval:
Optimal Engine has four ways to read memory, from a plain search to a governed context package for an agent.

| Call | Returns | Use it for |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/search` | Ranked results with their sources | Finding things |
| `GET /api/grep` | Matching chunks, with intent, scale, and modality filters | Finding exact passages |
| `POST /api/rag` (`optimal ask`) | A context envelope sized for a reader, with sources | Giving a model what it needs to answer one question |
| `POST /api/assemble` (`optimal assemble`) | A tiered context package with reviewed facts and memories | Briefing an agent before it acts |

None of them writes an answer with a language model.
They return context and the sources it came from; your model writes the answer.

## Search

```bash
curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:4200/api/search?q=renewal&workspace=default:notes&limit=10&mode=auto" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPTIMAL_ENGINE_API_KEY"
```

| Parameter | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `q` | required | Query |
| `workspace` | `default` | Workspace id |
| `limit`, `offset` | `10`, `0` | Paging |
| `mode` | `auto` | `auto`, `lexical`, or `hybrid` |
| `type` | all | `memory` searches only durable memories |
| `as_of` | now | ISO 8601 instant to measure recency against |

Each result has an `id`, `title`, `uri`, `content`, a short `l0_abstract`, a `score`, and the `workspace_id` it came from.
`inherited: true` marks a result that came from the organization policy rather than the workspace itself.

### How ranking works

- **Full-text**: SQLite FTS5 BM25, multiplied by a recency decay that depends on the kind of source and by a signal-quality score.
- **Vector**: cosine similarity over embeddings, when an embedding model is set up.
- **Hybrid**: a weighted mix of the two, then a boost for results connected in the graph.

| `mode` | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `auto` | Uses vectors when the embedding model answers, and full-text otherwise |
| `lexical` | Full-text only |
| `hybrid` | Requires vectors; answers `503 hybrid_unavailable` instead of quietly falling back |

Ties are broken by `uri` and then `id`, so the same query on the same data returns the same order.

> **Note: Vector scale**
>
> Vectors are stored in SQLite and compared in the Engine process, without an approximate nearest-neighbor index.
> Vector search time grows with the number of chunks, so watch `search_latency_ms` in [metrics](/docs/optimal-engine/operations#observability) as a workspace grows.

## Ask

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4200/api/rag \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPTIMAL_ENGINE_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"query": "What did we decide about pricing?", "workspace": "default:notes", "format": "claude", "bandwidth": "small"}'
```

The Engine reads the intent of the question, looks for a curated wiki page first, searches when there is none, and fits the result to the reader.

| Field | Values |
|---|---|
| `format` | `plain`, `markdown`, `claude`, `openai` |
| `bandwidth` | `small`, `medium`, `large` |
| `strategy` | `tiered`, `reconstructive`, `hybrid` |
| `audience` | Who will read it, used to filter and shape the result |
| `context_package` | `true` returns a governed context package as well |

```json
{
  "source": "chunks",
  "envelope": {
    "body": "...",
    "format": "claude",
    "sources": ["optimal://..."],
    "warnings": []
  },
  "trace": {"intent": "...", "n_candidates": 12, "n_delivered": 4, "elapsed_ms": 41}
}
```

`source` says where the context came from: `wiki`, `chunks`, `memory`, `context_package`, or `empty`.
`GET /api/rag/stream` returns the same steps as server-sent events: `intent`, `wiki_hit` or `chunks`, `composing`, `envelope`, and `done`.

## Assemble and reconstruct

`POST /api/assemble` returns what an agent should read before acting: tiers `l0` to `l3`, the `total_tokens`, the `sources`, and a `context_package`.
The context package holds reviewed facts and memory objects only, so a new source shows up there after its claims are promoted.

`POST /api/reconstruct` uses the reconstructive strategy: it expands across associations between memories the reader is allowed to see.
Associations can improve recall, but they never decide what is true.
Record how useful a reconstruction was with `POST /api/reconstruct/:id/outcome`, which the Engine credits per workspace and intent.

## Reviewing claims

```bash
optimal claims -w default:notes
optimal review -w default:notes
```

| Route | What it does |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/memory-core/claim-review` | The review queue |
| `GET /api/memory-core/claims` | Claims, with their status and sources |
| `POST /api/memory-core/claims/:id/promote` | Accept a claim as a fact (`claims:review`) |
| `POST /api/memory-core/claims/:id/reject` | Reject a claim (`claims:review`) |

The default rule promotes a claim on its own when its score reaches the workspace threshold of 0.85.
Set `OPTIMAL_CLAIM_PROMOTION_MODE=manual` to review every claim yourself.

## Versioned memories

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4200/api/memory/remember \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPTIMAL_ENGINE_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"workspace": "default:notes", "content": "Customer Example Co renews in March."}'
```

`remember` scores the memory first and answers with an `action`:

| `action` | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `add` | Stored as a new memory |
| `update` | Stored as a new version of a similar memory |
| `skip` | Already known; nothing changed |
| `pending_claim` | Proposed as a claim for review |
| `rejected` | Below the gate |

The `gate` object explains the score: `novelty`, `salience`, `prediction_error`, and `reason`.
`POST /api/memory` stores a memory without the gate.

| Route | What it does |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/memory` | List, with `q`, `include_forgotten`, and paging |
| `GET /api/memory/:id/versions` | The version chain |
| `GET /api/memory/:id/relations` | Links: `updates`, `extends`, `derives`, `contradicts`, `cites` |
| `POST /api/memory/:id/update`, `extend`, `derive` | A new linked version |
| `POST /api/memory/:id/forget` | Hide it; the row stays |
| `DELETE /api/memory/:id` | Delete it permanently |

## Time travel

`search`, `grep`, `ask`, and `assemble` take `as_of`, an ISO 8601 instant.
Facts carry the time they are valid for, and a superseded fact stays readable as history.

## Benchmarks

On LoCoMo, all 1,540 questions, the Engine's candidate portfolio retrieves at least one gold evidence item for 96.1% of questions and 87.1% of all gold evidence at top 100.
That measures retrieval, not answer accuracy.
The candidate portfolio is opt-in (`memory_search_mode=portfolio` on a memory search); the default memory search is `hybrid`.
The repository's README has the full results, their limits, and the commands that reproduce them under `benchmarks/`.
optimal-engine/miosa:
On MIOSA, an Optimal Engine runs as a managed database with the engine `optimal`.
MIOSA creates and runs it for you: you never install it, hold its admin key, or take its backups by hand.

## Availability

Managed Engines are enabled per organization.
Until yours is enabled:

- the console's create flow under **Databases** does not offer Optimal Engine;
- **Start Memory** answers "Memory could not be started. Your role may not allow it, or Memory is not set up for this organization yet.";
- creating one over the API or CLI answers `422` with the code `ENGINE_NOT_AVAILABLE`.

To have it turned on, open a ticket from the console or email [support@miosa.ai](mailto:support@miosa.ai) with your organization's name.
See [Support](/docs/faq/support).
Self-hosting needs no enablement; see the [quickstart](/docs/optimal-engine/quickstart).

## What you get

| Part | Detail |
|---|---|
| Machine | A private machine in your workspace's network, reachable only inside MIOSA and through the MIOSA API |
| Data | A durable data disk that survives restarts and upgrades |
| Keys | MIOSA holds the Engine's admin key and never shows it; you mint short-lived client keys |
| Workspaces | An Engine workspace named after each MIOSA workspace attached to it |
| Backups | Scheduled backups of the whole data disk, and backups on demand |
| Health | Health checks reported by the Engine itself |
| Search | Full-text search. Managed Engines do not include an embedding model, so vector search is not available on MIOSA. |

It is billed like an always-on managed database while it runs, at the hourly price of its size.
The console shows that price, and the price for a full month, before it creates anything.

## Workspace Memory in the console

**Optimal > Memory** (`/optimal/memory`) is the simplest way in.
Memory belongs to one workspace: pick a workspace in the switcher first.

1. Press **Start Memory**.
   - If your organization already has a running Engine, Memory attaches this workspace to it at no new cost.
   - Otherwise the console offers to create one with 1 vCPU, 2 GiB of memory, and the smallest disk, and shows its price. Press **Create and start Memory**.
2. "Memory is starting. This takes about a minute."
3. When it is running, the page has a search box over everything the workspace knows, with each result's title, location, and an excerpt.

To add to Memory, ask Optimal in a chat to save a note.

## How Optimal chat uses Memory

When the workspace has Memory, [Optimal](/docs/optimal) can:

- **search it** before answering about the workspace's people, projects, clients, or history, and say so when Memory has nothing;
- **save** a note, a decision, or a transcript you ask it to keep;
- **start** Memory for the workspace when you ask.

In an **All workspaces** chat, Optimal searches every workspace you can open and names the workspace each result came from.

Each chat also has a Memory panel:

- **Save to memory** stores the chat as a session.
- **Sources** lists what Optimal read, grouped by workspace in an organization chat.
- **Learned in this chat** lists the claims the chat produced; accept or reject each one.

Optimal reaches Memory through MIOSA as you, with your permissions.
It holds no Engine key and has no network path to the Engine.
What Memory returns is passed to the model as untrusted content.

## From a terminal

The [MIOSA CLI](/docs/cli) has a `miosa engine` command group, version 2.3.19 or newer.

```bash
miosa engine create brain --workspace notes --for workspace --wait
miosa engine list
miosa engine status notes
```

`create` returns the existing Engine when one with that name exists, so scripts can call it every time.
`--for` picks a starting size: `agent` (tiny, 2 GiB disk), `workspace` (xs, 10 GiB), or `business` (small, 25 GiB).
`--size tiny|xs|small|medium|large` and `--disk <GiB>` override it.
An Engine created for a workspace attaches to that workspace when it first runs.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `miosa engine attach <workspace> --to <engine>` | Attach another workspace to an Engine |
| `miosa engine detach <workspace>` | Detach a workspace and revoke its Engine key |
| `miosa engine status [workspace]` | Which Engine serves a workspace, or every Engine and its workspaces |
| `miosa engine connect <engine>` | Mint a client key and write an `optimal` CLI profile |
| `miosa engine shell <engine> [-- command]` | Run a shell or a command with a key that is revoked when it exits |
| `miosa engine backup <engine>`, `miosa engine backups <engine>` | Take a backup now, or list backups |
| `miosa engine recover <engine>` | Restore a backup over the Engine, or with `--to-new <name>` into a new one |
| `miosa engine upgrade <engine> --to <version>`, `miosa engine rollback <engine>` | Change the Engine version |
| `miosa engine rm <engine>` | Delete the Engine and its data disk |

### Use the optimal CLI and MCP server

`miosa engine connect` mints a read/write key for one of the Engine's workspaces and writes `~/.config/optimal/profile` with mode `0600`.
The [`optimal` CLI and MCP server](/docs/optimal-engine/cli-sdks-mcp) read that profile, so they reach the managed Engine with no other setup.

```bash
miosa engine connect brain                       # key lasts 24 hours
miosa engine connect brain --workspace notes --profile notes --ttl 72h
optimal boot
optimal search "renewal"
miosa engine shell brain -- optimal brief        # one command, key revoked after
```

`--print` prints shell exports instead of writing a profile.
Keys last 24 hours by default and at most 30 days.

## Machines in the workspace

Sandboxes, computers, apps, and agents in a workspace attached to an Engine start with two variables:

| Variable | Value |
|---|---|
| `OPTIMAL_ENGINE_URL` | The Engine's private address, on port 4200 |
| `OPTIMAL_ENGINE_API_KEY` | A key limited to that workspace |

The `optimal` CLI and the MCP server read both, so an agent on the machine can call `optimal boot` straight away.
A machine still starts when the Engine is down.

## Call the Engine API

From outside the workspace, call the Engine through MIOSA with a client key.

1. Mint a client key. Only an organization owner or admin can mint one.

   ```bash
   curl -s -X POST https://api.miosa.ai/api/v1/databases/$ENGINE_ID/client-keys \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $MIOSA_API_KEY" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"workspace_id": "your_workspace_id", "ttl_seconds": 86400}'
   ```

   `201` returns `data.key` once, with its `id` and `expires_at`.
   The workspace must be attached to the Engine.
   `GET /databases/:id/client-keys` lists keys without their secrets, and `DELETE /databases/:id/client-keys/:key_id` revokes one.

2. Call the Engine with it:

   ```bash
   curl -s "https://api.miosa.ai/api/v1/engines/$ENGINE_ID/engine-api/api/search?q=renewal" \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $ENGINE_CLIENT_KEY"
   ```

The proxy forwards only the routes an agent needs, and answers `404` for everything else, including key, sync, backup, and maintenance routes.

| Method | Routes under `/api/` |
|---|---|
| `GET` | `boot`, `brief`, `protocol`, `operating-projection`, `rhythm/current`, `loops`, `search`, `grep`, `read`, `memory`, `memory-core/claims`, `memory-core/claim-review`, `sessions`, `sessions/:id`, `org-policy`, `review/routing`, `routing/rules`, `authority/effective`, `viability`, `viability/history`, `analyses`, `jobs`, `workspaces`, `status`, `health`, `version`, `profile`, `recall/:kind`, `wiki/:slug`, `render/specs`, `agent-actions/:id` |
| `POST` | `rag`, `assemble`, `reconstruct`, `ingest`, `memory`, `memory/remember`, `memory/:id/forget`, `loops`, `loops/extract`, `loops/:id/:action`, `sessions/commit`, `routing/classify`, `signals/check`, `authority/decide`, `authority/requests`, `agent-actions`, `render/context` |

| Status | Code | When |
|---|---|---|
| 404 | `NOT_FOUND` | The route is not on the list |
| 409 | `ENGINE_NOT_RUNNING` | The Engine is stopped or starting |
| 413 | `REQUEST_TOO_LARGE` | The body is over 1 MiB, or the query string over 8 KiB |
| 502 | `ENGINE_UNAVAILABLE`, `ENGINE_RESPONSE_TOO_LARGE` | The Engine did not answer, or answered too much |

### Workspace Memory routes

These use your MIOSA API key, not a client key, and reach the Engine that serves the workspace.

All paths start with `https://api.miosa.ai/api/v1/workspaces/:workspace_id/engine`.

| Route | What it does | Permission |
|---|---|---|
| `GET .../engine` | Which Engine serves the workspace | |
| `GET .../engine/search?q=&limit=` | Search the workspace's Memory | `databases:read` |
| `GET .../engine/boot` | The workspace's boot briefing | `databases:read` |
| `POST .../engine/remember` with `{"content", "metadata"}` | Save a memory | `databases:write` |
| `POST .../engine/sessions` with `{"correlation_id", "messages", "title"}` | Save a chat as a session | `databases:write` |
| `GET .../engine/sessions/:session_id` | Read a saved chat | `databases:read` |
| `POST .../engine/claims/:claim_id/accept` or `/reject` | Review a claim | `databases:write` |

A workspace with no Engine answers `404 NOT_FOUND`; an Engine that is not running answers `409 ENGINE_NOT_RUNNING`.

## Backups, upgrades, and size

Open the Engine under **Databases** in the console.
Its page has an **Overview** tab with the connection, health, and usage against the size's limits, a **Backups** tab, a **Resize** button, and, when the Engine reports them, **Brief**, **Loops**, **Workspaces**, and **Keys** tabs.

| Size | vCPU | Memory | Disk |
|---|---|---|---|
| `agent` | 1 | 1 GiB | 2 GiB |
| `workspace` | 1 | 2 GiB | 10 GiB |
| `business` | 2 | 4 GiB | 25 GiB |
| `platform` | 4 | 8 GiB | 100 GiB |
| `scale` | 8 | 16 GiB | 250 GiB |

Resizing moves between `workspace`, `business`, `platform`, and `scale`; `agent` is a starting size only.
A resize refuses a size whose disk or memory cannot hold what the Engine already uses, and restarts a running Engine.
Over the API, `POST /api/v1/databases/:id/resize` takes `{"size": "business"}`, and `"dry_run": true` returns the plan without changing anything.

`miosa engine recover --to-new` restores a backup into a new Engine and never touches the original.
Restoring over the Engine keeps the previous data aside; `GET /api/v1/databases/:id/restore-copies` lists those copies.

> **Note: Self-hosted and managed together**
>
> A managed Engine is the same software as a self-hosted one, so the [API](/docs/optimal-engine/api), the [CLI](/docs/optimal-engine/cli-sdks-mcp), and the [concepts](/docs/optimal-engine/concepts) apply to both.
optimal-engine/operations:
This page is for a self-hosted Engine.
On MIOSA, backups, upgrades, and resizing are done for you; see [Optimal Engine on MIOSA](/docs/optimal-engine/miosa#backups-upgrades-and-size).

## Backups

A backup is an online copy of the SQLite database, taken with `VACUUM INTO` while the Engine keeps serving.

```bash
mix optimal.backup /var/backups/engine-$(date +%F).db --verify
```

`--verify` runs an integrity check on the copy.
Over HTTP, an `admin` key can call `POST /api/backup` with an optional `{"name"}`; the file is written in the backup folder and the response has its `path`, `size_bytes`, `checksum_sha256`, and `integrity_status`.

### Offsite backups

With `OPTIMAL_BACKUP_KEY` and the `OPTIMAL_S3_*` settings, backups can be encrypted and sent to S3-compatible storage:

```bash
mix optimal.backup /tmp/snapshot.db --offsite
mix optimal.backup --list-offsite
```

Set `OPTIMAL_OFFSITE_BACKUP_INTERVAL_MS` (60000 or more) to take them on a schedule.
The Engine keeps the newest 14 offsite and 3 local copies by default (`OPTIMAL_OFFSITE_BACKUP_KEEP`, `OPTIMAL_OFFSITE_BACKUP_KEEP_LOCAL`).

### Restore

Stop the Engine first.

```bash
mix optimal.restore /var/backups/engine-2026-10-23.db
mix optimal.restore --from-offsite <backup id>
```

The restore checks the copy's checksum and integrity before it changes anything, and keeps the previous database beside it as `<db>.pre-restore-<time>`.

> **Caution: What a backup does not include**
>
> A backup is the database only.
> Workspace folders under `OPTIMAL_ENGINE_ROOT`, local asset files, and the RocksDB graph folder are not in it; back them up with the volume or folder.
> Local backups are not encrypted, and they contain the encrypted connector keys, so store them as secrets.
> With Docker, the simplest full backup is the whole `/data` volume.

## Upgrades

1. Take a backup.
2. Install the new version: pull the new tag and rebuild, or start the new image on the same volume.
3. Start it. Migrations run at boot, each in its own transaction, before the API answers.

If a migration fails, it is rolled back, the Engine refuses to open the store, and it exits with `migration <number> failed and was rolled back: <cause>`.
Migrations that ran before it in the same boot stay applied, so going back means restoring the backup from step 1.

Check what is running and what it expects:

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4200/api/version -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPTIMAL_ENGINE_API_KEY"
mix optimal.migrate --status
```

`mix optimal.conformance --url <url> --key <key>` runs the conformance suite against a live Engine, prints a JSON report, and exits non-zero on any failure, so it can gate an upgrade.

A release build runs the same maintenance with the API off: `bin/optimal maintenance migrate`, `health`, `embed_backfill`, `graph_backfill`, `facts`, or `claims`.
It exits `0` when done, `1` on failure, and `78` when the Engine is in the wrong state for the task.

## Sizing

`OPTIMAL_SIZE_PROFILE` sets the rate limit per key and the advised limits the Engine measures itself against.

| Profile | Machine | Disk | Vectors | Memories | API requests per minute per key |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `agent` | 1 vCPU, 1 GiB | 2 GiB | 50,000 | 100,000 | 300 |
| `workspace` | 1 vCPU, 2 GiB | 10 GiB | 250,000 | 500,000 | 600 |
| `business` (default) | 2 vCPU, 4 GiB | 25 GiB | 1M | 2M | 1,200 |
| `platform` | 4 vCPU, 8 GiB | 100 GiB | 5M | 10M | 3,000 |
| `scale` | 8 vCPU, 16 GiB or more | 250 GiB or more | more | more | 6,000 |

The vector and memory numbers are advice, not hard caps.
At 70% of any of them, `GET /api/storage` and `/api/metrics` recommend the next profile.
A key can get its own rate limit with `rate_limit_per_minute` in its metadata.

The Engine is a single writer: run one Engine per data folder.

## Replication

Two SQLite Engines can keep a workspace in sync.

| Route | What it does |
|---|---|
| `POST /api/sync/enable` | Start recording changes in a workspace |
| `POST /api/sync/peers` | Add a peer: `{"workspace", "url", "api_key", "policy", "max_class"}` (`admin`) |
| `POST /api/sync/run` | Sync now |
| `GET /api/sync/status`, `/changes`, `/conflicts` | State, the change log, and conflicts |
| `POST /api/sync/conflicts/:id/resolve` | Resolve one conflict |

`policy` is `push`, `pull`, `both`, or `none`.
`max_class` is the most sensitive data class that may leave: `public`, `internal`, `confidential` (default), or `restricted`.
The peer's key is stored encrypted with `CONNECTOR_KEY`.
Peers sync every 20 seconds by default.
Assets, connectors, API keys, jobs, and tools are not replicated.

## Move a workspace

A workspace bundle is one file with a whole workspace in it.

| Route | What it does |
|---|---|
| `POST /api/workspaces/:id/bundle` | Write a bundle |
| `POST /api/bundles/import` | Import one |
| `POST /api/bundles/jobs/export`, `POST /api/bundles/jobs/import` | The same as background jobs, for large workspaces |
| `GET /api/bundles/jobs/:id` | Follow a job |
| `POST /api/workspaces/:id/finalize-move` | Remove the workspace from the old Engine after the move |

Bundles are limited to 5 GiB (`OPTIMAL_BUNDLE_MAX_BYTES`).

## Erasure and retention

```bash
mix optimal.compliance dsar <principal id>
mix optimal.compliance erase <principal id> --preview
mix optimal.compliance erase <principal id>
mix optimal.compliance hold place <signal id> --by <actor> --reason "litigation"
mix optimal.compliance hold list
mix optimal.compliance retention sweep --dry-run
```

| Action | Effect |
|---|---|
| `dsar` | Exports what the Engine holds about one person |
| `erase` | Deletes it, and what was derived from it. `--preview` shows what would go; `--force` overrides legal holds. |
| `hold` | Places, lists, or releases a legal hold that stops deletion |
| `retention sweep` | Applies each source's retention rule |
| `POST /api/workspaces/:id/archive` | Archives a workspace; its rows are kept |

An erasure does not reach backups, offsite copies, exported bundles, or replicas that already synced the data.
SQLite does not overwrite freed pages, so deleted text can remain in the database file until it is vacuumed.

## Observability

| Route | What it returns |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/health` | `up`, `degraded`, or `down`, with the check that failed |
| `GET /api/metrics` | JSON counters, latencies, connector state, and size gauges |
| `GET /api/metrics/prometheus` | Prometheus text, such as `optimal_engine_search_latency_ms`, `optimal_engine_memories_total`, `optimal_engine_uptime_seconds` |
| `GET /api/viability` | A report on the workspace as an operating system, with alerts |

The Prometheus route needs a key when keys are required; it is only exempt from rate limits.
`deploy/grafana-dashboard.json` in the repository is a ready dashboard for it.
Logs go to standard output as `[level] message`.
optimal-engine/quickstart:
This guide runs one Engine on your machine, creates a workspace, stores a source, and finds it again.
It takes about ten minutes, most of it the first compile.
To use a managed Engine on MIOSA instead, skip to [On MIOSA](/docs/optimal-engine/quickstart#on-miosa).

You end with:

- an Engine on `http://127.0.0.1:4200`;
- an API key that scopes every request;
- a workspace `default:notes` with one stored source;
- a search result that points back to that source.

## 1. Run the Engine

**From a checkout**

You need Erlang/OTP 27 or newer, Elixir 1.17 or newer, git, and a C toolchain.
On macOS, also run `brew install snappy`.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Miosa-osa/OptimalEngine.git
cd OptimalEngine
mix deps.get
```

Mint the first key before the server starts.
The key is printed once, so copy it now.

```bash
mix optimal.auth mint --name "root" --workspace '*'
```

Start the Engine with the HTTP API on and keys required:

```bash
OPTIMAL_API_ENABLED=true OPTIMAL_AUTH_REQUIRED=true mix run --no-halt
```

The first start runs every database migration before the API answers.

**With Docker**

You need Docker.
The first image build compiles RocksDB and can take 30 to 60 minutes.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Miosa-osa/OptimalEngine.git
cd OptimalEngine
docker build -f deploy/Dockerfile.engine \
  --build-arg OPTIMAL_RELEASE_CHANNEL=stable \
  -t optimal-engine:quickstart .
```

Mint the first key in a one-off container that opens the same volume with the API off:

```bash
docker run --rm -v optimal-data:/data -e OPTIMAL_API_ENABLED=false optimal-engine:quickstart \
  /app/bin/optimal eval \
  'OptimalEngine.Auth.ApiKey.mint(%{tenant_id: "default", name: "root", scopes: ["*"], workspace_scope: ["*"]}) |> IO.inspect()'
```

Start the Engine.
`OPTIMAL_ENGINE_API_KEY` is the key you just minted; the container health check uses it.

```bash
docker run -d --name optimal-engine -p 127.0.0.1:4200:4200 \
  -v optimal-data:/data \
  -e OPTIMAL_AUTHORITY_KEY="$(openssl rand -hex 32)" \
  -e CONNECTOR_KEY="$(openssl rand -hex 32)" \
  -e OPTIMAL_ENGINE_API_KEY="<your key>" \
  optimal-engine:quickstart
```

The image turns on the API and requires keys by default.
Everything the Engine stores lives in the `optimal-data` volume, so replacing the container keeps your data.

## 2. Check that it answers

In a second terminal:

```bash
export OPTIMAL_ENGINE_API_KEY="<your key>"
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4200/api/health -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPTIMAL_ENGINE_API_KEY"
```

```json
{
  "status": "up",
  "live": true,
  "checks": {
    "store": ":ok",
    "migrations": ":ok",
    "credential_key": ":ok",
    "network_auth": ":ok"
  },
  "degraded": [],
  "warnings": []
}
```

`status` is `up`, `degraded` when there is a warning, or `down` when a check fails.
The real response also carries the release identity.

## 3. Create a workspace

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4200/api/workspaces \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPTIMAL_ENGINE_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"slug": "notes", "name": "Notes"}'
```

The response is the new workspace.
Its `id` is `default:notes`; use that id everywhere below.

## 4. Store a source

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4200/api/ingest \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPTIMAL_ENGINE_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "workspace": "default:notes",
    "title": "Supplier renewal call",
    "text": "Renewal call with the supplier moved to the 14th. The contract review is still open."
  }'
```

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "signal_id": "...",
  "genre": "...",
  "type": "...",
  "entities": [],
  "source_package_id": "..."
}
```

The Engine kept the source, classified it, and proposed claims from it.
A claim becomes a fact once it is reviewed or meets the workspace's promotion rule; see [Concepts](/docs/optimal-engine/concepts#claims-and-facts).

## 5. Search and ask

```bash
curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:4200/api/search?q=supplier%20renewal&workspace=default:notes&limit=5" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPTIMAL_ENGINE_API_KEY"
```

Each result has a `title`, the matching `content`, a `score`, and a `uri` in the `optimal://` scheme that points back to the source.

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4200/api/rag \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPTIMAL_ENGINE_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"query": "What is open with the supplier?", "workspace": "default:notes", "format": "markdown"}'
```

`envelope.body` is the context an answer should be written from, and `envelope.sources` lists the sources it used.
The Engine does not write the answer itself; hand the envelope to your model or agent.

> **Tip: Vector search is optional**
>
> Out of the box, search is full-text.
> Run [Ollama](https://ollama.com/) with `nomic-embed-text`, or point `OPTIMAL_EMBED_URL` at an embeddings endpoint, to add vector search.
> See [Install and configure](/docs/optimal-engine/install#embeddings).

## 6. Use the client CLI

The repository ships a small client CLI, `optimal` (also called `oe`), that needs only `sh`, `curl`, and `awk`.

```bash
apps/cli/install.sh
export OPTIMAL_ENGINE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4200
optimal doctor
optimal search "supplier renewal" -w default:notes
```

See [CLI, SDKs and MCP](/docs/optimal-engine/cli-sdks-mcp) for every command and for connecting an agent over MCP.

## On MIOSA

Managed Engines are enabled per organization.
Once yours is enabled:

1. Open **Optimal > Memory** in the console and pick a workspace.
2. Press **Start Memory**. The console shows the size and the hourly price before it creates anything.
3. When Memory is running, search it on the same page, or ask Optimal in a chat to save a note to Memory.

From a terminal, the [MIOSA CLI](/docs/cli) does the same:

```bash
miosa engine create notes-brain --workspace notes --for workspace --wait
miosa engine connect notes-brain
optimal search "supplier renewal"
```

See [Optimal Engine on MIOSA](/docs/optimal-engine/miosa) for what is included and how to ask for access.
optimal-engine/troubleshooting:
Each entry starts with what you see, then the fix.

## Start-up

### "Optimal Engine needs Erlang/OTP 27 or later"

The Engine uses the JSON module that ships with OTP 27.
Install OTP 27 or newer; avoid 28.0 to 28.2.

### The Engine starts but nothing listens on port 4200

The HTTP API is off unless `OPTIMAL_API_ENABLED=true`.
Set it and start again.
`mix optimal.api` alone prints a listening line without turning the API on, so set the variable for it too.

### "OPTIMAL_AUTH_REQUIRED must be true or false"

A setting has a value the Engine does not accept, and the boot stops.
The message names the variable; fix its value.
The same applies to `OPTIMAL_EMBED_URL`, `OPTIMAL_SIZE_PROFILE`, `OPTIMAL_ENGINE_SCOPE`, and the other settings in [Install and configure](/docs/optimal-engine/install#settings).

### "migration ... failed and was rolled back"

An upgrade's migration failed.
The Engine will not open the store until it is fixed.
Restore the backup you took before the upgrade, then start the previous version; see [Operations](/docs/optimal-engine/operations#upgrades).

### The Docker container stays "unhealthy"

The health check calls `/api/health` with `OPTIMAL_ENGINE_API_KEY`, and keys are required in the image.
Set `OPTIMAL_ENGINE_API_KEY` on the container to a valid key.

## Health

`GET /api/health` reports `status` and the checks behind it.

| Warning or error | Fix |
|---|---|
| `store_unreachable` | The database file cannot be opened. Check `OPTIMAL_ENGINE_DB`, the disk, and file permissions. |
| `migrations_pending` | Restart the Engine so it applies them, or run `mix optimal.migrate`. |
| `connector_key_missing` | You set up a connector or a replication peer without `CONNECTOR_KEY`. Set it to 64 hex characters. |
| `auth_open_on_network` | The Engine is bound beyond loopback with keys off. Set `OPTIMAL_AUTH_REQUIRED=true`. |
| `embedder_unreachable`, `embedder_unauthorized`, `embedder_dimension_mismatch` | Shown with `?full=true`. Check `OLLAMA_HOST` or `OPTIMAL_EMBED_URL`, its key, and `OPTIMAL_EMBED_DIMENSIONS`. |

## Requests

### 401 `missing_api_key` on every call, including `/api/health`

Keys are required.
Send `Authorization: Bearer <key>`.
Mint the first key with `mix optimal.auth mint`, or set `OPTIMAL_BOOTSTRAP_KEY`.

### 403 `workspace_scope_denied`

The key does not cover that workspace.
Check its workspaces with `GET /api/auth/whoami`, and mint a key that includes the workspace.

### 400 `workspace_required`

The key is limited to named workspaces and the request named none.
Pass `workspace`, or `-w` in the CLI.

### Search returns nothing for something you just stored

- Use the same full workspace id, such as `default:notes`, in every call.
  The Engine does not look up a bare slug such as `notes`; it treats it as a different workspace id.
- A context package from `assemble` holds reviewed facts only; a new source shows up there after its claims are promoted.
  Use `search` to see sources right away.

### 503 `hybrid_unavailable`

`mode=hybrid` needs an embedding model, and none answered.
Use `mode=auto`, which falls back to full-text, or set up embeddings; see [Install and configure](/docs/optimal-engine/install#embeddings).

### 503 `busy` with `Retry-After: 1`

The store was busy, often right after boot or during a long write.
Retry after the delay.

### 429 `rate_limited`

The key used its budget for the minute.
Wait `retry_after_ms`, or raise the size profile or the key's `rate_limit_per_minute`; see [Operations](/docs/optimal-engine/operations#sizing).

### 426 `client_incompatible`

The `optimal` CLI or MCP server is of a different major version than the Engine.
Update the client from the same release as the Engine.

## On MIOSA

### "Memory could not be started"

Your organization does not have managed Engines enabled, or your role cannot create databases.
See [Availability](/docs/optimal-engine/miosa#availability).

### 422 `ENGINE_NOT_AVAILABLE`

Managed Engines are not enabled for your organization.
Contact support to have them turned on.

### 409 `ENGINE_NOT_RUNNING`

The Engine is stopped or still starting.
Start it from **Databases**, or wait about a minute after creating it.

### 404 `NOT_FOUND` from the engine-api proxy

The route is not one a client key may call, or the workspace has no Engine.
See the allowed routes in [Optimal Engine on MIOSA](/docs/optimal-engine/miosa#call-the-engine-api).
Key, backup, sync, and maintenance routes are managed through MIOSA instead.

### A client key stopped working

Client keys expire, after 24 hours by default.
Run `miosa engine connect <engine>` again, and restart the MCP server, which reads its key once at start.
